name: Child Sexual Abuse Directive
impact_assessment: SEC(2009) 355 (prepared for the 2009 Framework Decision proposal)
evidence_rating: thin: Commission transposition reports (2016) and a 2022 evaluation annexed to the recast impact assessment
summary: The Commission's 2016 reports found substantive progress in national criminal law but gaps in prevention programmes, victim support and the removal of abuse material online. Its 2022 evaluation, supported by an external study (RAND Europe and EY), concluded that even full transposition would not address the problem adequately, leading to the 2024 recast proposal. Comparable data on offences do not exist.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below
Prevent abuse, protect victims, prosecute offenders
indicators.evidence: 2016: main gaps in offender programmes (Arts 22-24), substantive criminal law (Arts 3-5) and victim support (Arts 18-20); removal of online material (Art. 25) still incomplete.

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Report assessing the extent to which the Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive 2011/93/EU, COM(2016) 871
literature.title: Report assessing the extent to which the Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive 2011/93/EU
literature.headline: Substantive progress in criminal codes and cooperation; main gaps in offender programmes, substantive criminal law and victim assistance; no plan to amend
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found that countries had changed their criminal laws but lagged on prevention programmes and support for child victims.

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Report assessing the implementation of the measures referred to in Article 25 of Directive 2011/93/EU (websites containing child sexual abuse material), COM(2016) 872
literature.title: Report assessing the implementation of the measures referred to in Article 25 of Directive 2011/93/EU (websites containing child sexual abuse material)
literature.outcomes: removal and blocking of abuse material online
literature.headline: Significant efforts by Member States; prompt removal of material hosted in their territory and safeguards for blocking still to be ensured
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found that removing child abuse material from websites was still not prompt enough everywhere.

literature.citation: European Commission (2024), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children (recast), with the evaluation of Directive 2011/93/EU, SWD(2024) 33
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children (recast), with the evaluation of Directive 2011/93/EU
literature.method: ex-post evaluation (external study by RAND Europe and EY) within impact assessment
literature.headline: Evaluation found that even with full transposition, child sexual abuse is not adequately addressed; prevention and victim-assistance programmes rarely evaluated by Member States
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's evaluation concluded that the 2011 rules, even if fully applied, were not enough to tackle child sexual abuse, especially online.
